original_source_text: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are widely used in hardware security but vulnerable to adversarial netlist rewrites. Existing adversarial approaches incur high overheads. We present NetDeTox, an automated framework combining large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning (RL) for efficient rewriting. The RL agent identifies GNN-critical components while the LLM devises functionality-preserving rewrites that diversify motifs. Iterative feedback minimizes overheads. Compared to state-of-the-art AttackGNN, NetDeTox degrades all security schemes with fewer rewrites and substantially lower area overheads (54.50%, 25.44%, and 41.04% reductions for GNN-RE, GNN4IP, and OMLA). For larger circuits, NetDeTox even reduces original area, demonstrating practical scalability.
